hero.caption: GITMO stone plaque in the Washington National Cathedral. Donated in 1965 by the officers and enlisted men of the United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, which is often incorrectly refered to as as GITMO when in fact it is abbreviated as GTMO, in appreciation for the visit of Rev. Francis B. Sayre Jr., dean of the cathedral for 27 years, in July 1964. Sayre was the the first grandchild of President Woodrow Wilson and served as a Navy chaplain during World War II.
hero.alt: GITMO stone plaque in the Washington National Cathedral. Donated in 1965 by the officers and enlisted men of the United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, which is often incorrectly refered to as as GITMO when in fact it is abbreviated as GTMO, in appreciation for the visit of Rev. Francis B. Sayre Jr., dean of the cathedral for 27 years, in July 1964. Sayre was the the first grandchild of President Woodrow Wilson and served as a Navy chaplain during World War II.

At left top, Jackson reading the Bible in Confederate camp; left bottom, teaching (using a w:compass (drawing tool)) in w:Virginia Military Institute; bottom right, w:Mexican-American War; upper right, Jackson enters heaven. The windows were removed in 2017.[1]
